verdict: Conditional accounting with optional unestimated experiments. Not a forecast or comprehensive welfare estimate.

inputs.finding: CSO Annual National Accounts 2023 reports €290.9bn. This is the recorded release vintage, not a claim about the latest revision.
Uses the recorded £63.3bn project anchor and divides by verified 2023 GBP-per-EUR .86979. The official GDP cell and vintage remain unverified, so this anchor supports experiments only.
Uses the original sterling figures, ONS L8GG calendar-year averages for 2019 and 2023, and the reciprocal of the verified annual ECB reference rate. No reverse conversion of rounded euro totals.
ONS L8GG FY2022–23 to CY2023 conversion with recorded 2023 FX. Whether this is the correct fiscal period of the frozen study observations remains unresolved.
Doyle 2025 Table 1 reports revenue £21.773bn. The same assumed FY conversion as the frozen bridge is used. Exact official release and cell need confirmation.
Opening revenue plus the frozen €17.058bn deficit. It reconciles exactly to the project deficit and approximates the separately rebased study spending figure within source rounding.
F&M 2024 Table 6 gives a 2019 gross pay increment of £4.306bn. It is separately rebased, not inferred from a net fiscal envelope or treated as a current wage-policy costing.
F&M 2024 Table 6 gives a 2019 gross welfare increment of £4.809bn. Eligibility, composition and future rates still require programme costing.
F&M 2024 Table 6 reports a 2019 current public pay bill of £6.797bn. It is a historical normalisation, not a newly measured Northern Ireland pay bill.
Doyle 2025 Table 1 and Table 2 contain £14.220bn. Table 2 labels the period 2019 while Table 1 and surrounding text say 2023. The official update remains on hold.

Doyle 2025 Table 2 reports £5.722bn. The same frozen envelope now defines both immediate transfer and the endpoint of phased funding transfer, without mixing a net incremental allowance with a different gross endpoint.
Doyle 2025 Table 2 reports £3.533bn. It remains a frozen annual interest-flow scenario, not an allocated inherited debt principal or refinancing forecast.
Doyle 2025 Table 2 reports £1.367bn. The accepted share starts at zero, and any assumed deduction is explicit. Replacement security and defence services still need costing.
Doyle 2025 Table 2 reports £0.400bn overseas and £0.177bn central costs. The accepted share starts at zero. Replacement functions and EU costs need a programme budget.
Doyle 2025 Table 2 combines £0.500bn HQ, £0.265bn central spending and £0.769bn tax/PRSI changes. The accepted share starts at zero. Attribution is not automatically additional cash revenue.

F&M 2024 Table 7 original sterling 2019 difference £18.104bn minus £9.577bn, converted directly with the UK deflator and recorded FX. The gap between this net increment and Table 6 gross components is kept visible rather than allocated to household income.
Accepted share of the study deduction, zero by default. A negotiation scenario, not an agreed saving.
Accepted share of the study central and overseas deductions, zero by default. Replacement functions remain a costing question.
Accepted share of study revenue adjustments, zero by default. This must be reconciled to the tax base and harmonisation assumptions.
Linear transfer of the same pension funding envelope. Forty years follows a stylised period discussed by Doyle, not a cohort forecast or agreed settlement.
Chosen policy output growth, not a treatment effect estimated from reunification. It must exclude the linked mechanisms and residual shocks to avoid counting gains twice.
Chosen Republic real GNI* path. It changes the denominator only and does not represent spillovers or financing effects on Republic activity.
Chosen harmonisation scope. Benefits, eligibility, staffing, hours and service quality are compressed into one envelope.
Chosen linear schedule. The source does not identify a single pay and welfare convergence process.
Preset spending choice. Capital versus current expenditure, additionality, maintenance and procurement capacity need separate budgets.
Preset recurring cost without a functional cost study or time-dependent transition budget.
Applies to the pension envelope and an explicitly supplied service base. Zero initially. It is not a demographic projection and must not duplicate baseline spending growth.
Constant real marginal borrowing rate. No debt-risk premium, maturity structure, inflation surprise or fiscal response.
Chosen real discount rate. Discounted financing-inclusive costs are a cash-flow measure, not a social welfare valuation.
Explicit real receipts path. Constant in real terms by default, not automatically tied to assumed output convergence.
Explicit real spending path. Constant in real terms by default. Any ageing already in this path must not be added again.
Explicit additional non-pension service spending exposed to ageing. Zero until a programme base is supplied. Excludes ageing already in baseline spending.
Explicit marginal revenue assumption. No average tax ratio is automatically treated as a causal tax elasticity.
Optional numerical scenario bound, disabled by default. It is not measured parity with the Republic. A run records when it binds.
Residual assumed output-level effect, not an FDI estimate. No firm entry, profit repatriation, trade model or corporation-tax base.

A separately assumed residual labour output contribution in either configuration, not output calculated from diagnostic job equivalents. It must exclude effects already represented by other mechanisms.
Chosen linear phase-in, not estimated business adjustment.
Chosen temporary output loss. No currency, banking, border, trade diversion or confidence model identifies its size.
Chosen linear recovery, not an estimated transition path.
Existing assets are an endowment. Prior taxation, forgone public investment and alternative uses are outside the horizon.
Deterministic real return without risk, fees or covariance with borrowing costs. A favourable return spread is not free fiscal capacity.
Asset acquisition, normally financed by taxes or borrowing. The model correctly adds financing needs but has no macro financing feedback.
Chosen saving horizon. No fiscal rule or legal mandate is represented.
Chosen withdrawal ceiling. Not a sustainable spending rule or guarantee of available assets.
Explicit split of additional expenditure. Starts at zero so current services and welfare never automatically become productive capital.
Chosen capacity margin. Starts at zero. Demand cannot create real output above the selected fixed-price capacity limit.
No estimated counterfactual or confidence interval. Distinguish output growth, productivity growth and population growth.
No NI project-level delivery estimate. Spending called investment also includes recurring health, education and welfare in Doyle Table 3, so it cannot all become productive physical capital.
Chosen timing with all expenditure completing at one lag. No project pipeline or distributed completion profile.
No asset mix or independently measured stock. Different public and private assets should not automatically share a depreciation rate.
No measured NI reference public capital stock. The elasticity cannot identify an output effect without a defensible stock denominator.
Bom and Ligthart report an average .106 across heterogeneous studies. It is not a NI causal coefficient and may overlap private-capital and employment responses added separately.
Unmeasured reference stock. Results depend on this scale and on whether the stock is gross or net.
Unestimated response. Public-capital effects may already include private adjustment, creating overlap.
Unestimated adjustment speed. The net additional stock now adjusts directly towards its target, with replacement implicit. It is a diagnostic and does not add another GDP effect.
Chosen Cobb–Douglas exponent, not an estimated NI capital share. It is used only for a private-productivity diagnostic and does not add to headline GDP.
A rebased historical pay-bill benchmark from F&M Table 6 replaces the invented normalisation. It is not a current measured NI pay bill or an estimate of private wage spillovers.
Illustrative after-tax share. Fiscal feedback from the pay increase has not been reconciled to the net harmonisation envelope.
No recipient-specific consumption estimate. Tax financing and displaced Republic spending are absent.
No recipient-specific consumption estimate or saving dynamics. Benefit eligibility and withdrawal rates are absent.
No input-output estimate of imports or flows between NI, the Republic and Great Britain. Domestic geography must be defined.
Unestimated spare-capacity closure. The first-round response is capped by the selected spare capacity. This is a fixed-price experiment, not a general-equilibrium closure.
Unestimated public-to-private wage transmission. Labour groups, occupations and regional wage bargaining are not represented.
The UCD paper does not estimate this aggregate NI coefficient. Household-specific wage elasticities cannot be directly treated as an aggregate employment effect.
Chosen income effect without benefit withdrawal or substitution effects. The income base is a hard-coded share of output.
Chosen response to a productivity-minus-wages index. No firm first-order conditions, labour share or NI estimation establish it.
No observed labour-force, hours, skills or participation constraint. Fixed reference employment does not grow with the baseline economy.
A diagnostic index only. No measured staff response, vacancy closure, staffing cost or public-service benefit.
Illustrative scale rather than verified employment. Additional jobs should be called job equivalents, not a forecast.
Migration responds only to unfilled jobs. Housing, departures, return migration, composition and fiscal incidence are omitted.
Chosen household scale with no age structure. No separate children, retirees or secondary earners.
Chosen marginal cost, not a budget costing. Housing, capital infrastructure and congestion are absent.
Off by default. Enabling this applies an assumed marginal revenue share to extra output, without claiming an estimated fiscal effect.
Negotiated scenario, not a settled legal or actuarial result. The current UI wording is qualified.
Negotiated scenario, not a settled allocation of debt stock, assets or interest.
After year seven the relative rate is capped at the lower of its previous rate and .4%. It cannot accelerate a low-growth path, but the timing and cap remain scenario assumptions.
Research configuration. Enabling links creates an illustrative mechanism experiment, not an estimated causal model.
Reporting choice rather than evidence. Long horizons magnify unsupported persistence, missing terminal liabilities and the output ceiling.

relationships.finding: The opening accounting reference has no negotiated deductions, no additional growth revenue and no linked behavioural effects. It is a conditional reference, not a best estimate of transition costs.
Net harmonisation uses original sterling Table 7 values directly. Gross pay and welfare use separate Table 6 values. All use the same recorded UK deflator and FX convention.
Gross pay and welfare no longer come from an arbitrary split of a net fiscal envelope. The source gross/net discrepancy is recorded without inventing its composition.
Separate gross receipts and spending paths reconcile to the frozen deficit. Growth in output does not silently generate revenue. Both real fiscal growth rates are explicit.
Each disputed defence, central-spending and revenue adjustment has an explicit accepted share, initially zero. The UK pension and debt switches are independent of policy labels.
A single pension envelope transfers linearly over the selected period. Phased and immediate transfer agree at the endpoint, without mixing gross and net conventions or claiming a cohort projection.
Ageing applies to pensions and an explicit non-pension service base. No arbitrary share of a residual deficit is aged and no residual balance disappears through composition.
Only the explicitly selected capital share of additional expenditure can become productive capital. That share starts at zero. Maintenance and project selection remain uncosted.
Public capital provides one reduced-form output effect. Induced private capital and jobs are diagnostics, not extra output multipliers stacked on that benchmark.
The additional net stock moves towards its target with replacement implicit. There is no second depreciation deduction preventing convergence to a fixed target.
Real demand effects cannot exceed selected spare capacity. The fixed-price experiment has no estimated price, trade, monetary or Republic-financing response.
The marginal revenue rate is adjustable and feedback is off initially. Policy growth and residual shocks must exclude effects entered in other channels.
There is no implicit doubling ceiling or claim of income parity. An optional user-selected bound records each binding year.
The switch never raises the relative growth rate after year seven. Its timing and remaining cap are still scenario settings.
Policy selection does not mutate liability switches. All compared bundles use the same negotiated terms, growth and structural settings. The selected comparison line uses exactly the main-run inputs.
A downloaded run includes policy inputs, shared settings, all compared bundles, annual results and the executable fingerprint. A CLI rejects mismatched models or results.
Contributions acquire assets and increase financing needs. Withdrawals reduce financing, not spending. Surpluses repay debt and excess becomes cash. Opening assets are not free income.
A constant annual interest allocation is not a negotiated debt stock. No inherited principal or refinancing model has been invented.
Wage spillovers, labour supply, welfare income effects and firm labour demand remain unestimated. Their indices cannot establish changes in employment or public-service quality.
Optional migration adds residents and service costs. No return migration, cohort ageing, housing constraint or complete migrant tax account is estimated.
UK status quo is zero only from the incremental Republic perspective. Shared Island allocates its extra expenditure to the Republic. No welfare ordering or constitutional causal effect follows.
The frozen ONS fiscal baseline and its exact official cells remain on hold. A historical harmonisation benchmark combined with a later deficit is a hybrid scenario, not an updated policy costing.
No probabilities, distributional microsimulation, banking model, currency changeover, trade model or complete all-island welfare analysis is supplied. Slider bounds are not confidence intervals.
